{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7805afafba4f3e37f761980184b3209bd1ef61ed7cb28ed7d807ea44ce65c49f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Regulatory signs","heading":"C — Regulatory signs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Regulatory signs

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Road signs fall into three main groups: regulatory, warning and guide signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs state actions that traffic law requires or forbids. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs can govern speed, traffic direction, turns and parking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Ignoring a regulatory sign can lead to a fine and driving-record points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Most regulatory signs are upright rectangles or squares with black-and-white coloring, though some also use red or are red and white. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
The highway STOP sign has a unique octagonal shape with eight sides. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
At a STOP sign, the driver must fully stop and check that pedestrians and cross traffic have cleared before proceeding. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Merely reducing speed at a STOP sign without completely stopping is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
When a stop line or crosswalk is marked, stop before the vehicle's front reaches the first painted line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
If traffic cannot be seen from the stopped position, first yield to pedestrians, then edge forward carefully for a clear view and proceed only after checking that traffic and pedestrians are clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
At an all-way stop, every approach must stop, and the vehicle arriving first should proceed first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
When two vehicles arrive together at an all-way stop, the driver on the left yields to the one on the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
Opposing drivers at an all-way stop may move cautiously together while watching for turns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A01
A YIELD sign is triangular with three sides. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A01
At a YIELD sign, reduce speed, check traffic and give priority to pedestrians and approaching cross traffic, stopping when necessary. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A01
Proceeding at a YIELD sign requires a safe gap that does not disrupt normal traffic flow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A01
A driver needs an adequate traffic gap before proceeding from either a STOP sign or a YIELD sign. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A01
A crossbuck marks the point where railroad tracks intersect the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A01
Treat a railroad crossbuck as a yield instruction, slowing and preparing to stop if an approaching train is seen or heard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
DO NOT ENTER warns against entering the one-way street or ramp from the direction of approach. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
WRONG WAY signs farther along a one-way street or ramp warn a driver who has entered against the permitted direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
A ONE WAY sign allows travel only in the direction of its arrow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A02
Driving against the direction of a one-way street creates a risk of a head-on collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A02
A divided highway consists of two one-way roadways separated by a median or guide rail. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A02
A DIVIDED HIGHWAY sign indicates that the current road intersects a divided highway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A02
At the divided-highway intersection described by the sign, the first roadway allows only a right turn and the second only a left turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A02
NO TRUCKS, NO BICYCLES and NO PEDESTRIAN CROSSING signs prohibit the indicated road user from using the posted roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A02
A NO U-TURN sign prohibits turning around to travel in the opposite direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A02
A NO RIGHT TURN sign forbids a right turn at the signed intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A02
A NO LEFT TURN sign forbids a left turn at the signed intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A02
A NO PARKING sign prohibits parking at the location where it is posted. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A02
DO NOT PASS prohibits passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A02
Directional lane-use signs at or near intersections show the maneuvers allowed from the lanes they control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A02
A left-turn-only lane requires a left turn, while an adjacent lane signed for left or straight permits either movement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A01
At a one-lane bridge or underpass, the supplemental sign used with YIELD tells drivers to give priority to opposing traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

Misconceptions: a posted limit describes ideal conditions rather than a safe speed for every condition; a turn-only lane still requires the indicated turn when entered by mistake.
Mnemonics: read the sign's command, apply it to the lane, and check for a required stop or yield.
Glossary: regulatory signs communicate legal duties; crossbuck marks a railroad crossing; median separates the opposing roadways of a divided highway.
